clauses.clause: sec. 1: establishes the White House Council for Community Solutions within CNCS
sec. 2: Council shall support the Call To Service campaign (identify solutions, recommend to President, honor leaders)
sec. 3: membership of up to 30 presidential appointees, Chair designation, 2-year terms
sec. 4: CNCS funds and supports the Council; agencies assist; no compensation, travel expenses; FACA functions to CNCS CEO
sec. 5: Council terminates 2 years from the order's date unless renewed by the President
sec. 6: general provisions (savings clauses, no enforceable rights)

moves.note: EO 13748 sec. 5 supersedes and revokes EO 13560 by name; read in the held FR printing.
Whole-order revocation ends every clause on 2016-11-16.
No open gap affects status; each proposition is quoted from a held official printing. Earlier own-terms termination in 2012 was not checked and only affects how early the first end is.

propositions.claim: The held text is the Federal Register printing of EO 13560 at 75 FR 78875.
propositions.quote: Executive Order 13560 of December 14, 2010 White House Council for Community Solutions

propositions.claim: Sec. 1 establishes the Council within CNCS.
propositions.quote: There is established the White House Council for Community Solutions (Council) within the Corporation for National and Community Service (CNCS)
The Council shall support the nationwide ‘‘Call To Service’’ campaign authorized in the Serve America Act (Public Law 111–13)
The Council shall be composed of not more than 30 members from outside the Federal Government appointed by the President.

propositions.claim: Sec. 4 directs CNCS to fund and support the Council.
propositions.quote: The CNCS shall provide funding and administrative support for the Council to the extent permitted by law and within existing appropriations.

propositions.claim: Sec. 5 sets a two-year termination for the Council unless renewed.
propositions.quote: The Council shall terminate 2 years from the date of this order, unless renewed by the President.

propositions.claim: EO 13748 sec. 5 expressly supersedes and revokes EO 13560 by name.
propositions.quote: This order supersedes Executive Order 13560 of December 14, 2010 (White House Council for Community Solutions), and Executive Order 13602 of March 15, 2012 [...] which are hereby revoked.

propositions.claim: The revoking order is EO 13748, dated 16 November 2016, printed at 81 FR 83619.
propositions.quote: Executive Order 13748 of November 16, 2016 Establishing a Community Solutions Council

propositions.claim: The U.S. Code note treats EO 13560 as superseded and revoked (quote taken from the evidence slice; the Code itself was not opened).
propositions.quote: which established the White House Council for Community Solutions, was superseded and revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 13748, § 5, Nov. 16, 2016, 81 F.R. 83621

review.conclusion_reason: EO 13748 section 5 expressly supersedes and revokes the whole named order on November 16, 2016, before the October 14, 2026 cutoff. This establishes NO operative status and revoked_or_superseded formal status for all six sections. The bounded ending claim does not require assuming that the conditional 2012 termination occurred. Section 6's savings and no-rights provisions were also checked in the held original.

verdicts.reason: Held EO_13560.txt prints the cited heading and Federal Register page 78875, volume 75.
Section 1 contains the quoted establishment within CNCS.
Section 2 contains the quoted campaign mandate and enumerates the summarized functions.
Section 3 confirms up to 30 outside presidential appointees, Chair designation and two-year terms; it additionally includes the CNCS Board Chair.
Section 4 confirms the funding quotation and the summarized assistance, compensation, travel and FACA provisions.
Section 5 contains the quoted conditional two-year termination verbatim.
Held EO_13748.txt, section 5, page 83621, expressly names EO 13560 in the supersession sentence ending 'which are hereby revoked.'
EO_13748.txt confirms the heading, November 16, 2016 date and opening page 83619. Section 5 appears on page 83621; these citations are compatible.

Independently confirmed the quoted Code note at https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/12653, Executive Documents, lines 148–149: 'was superseded and revoked'. Official Code retrieval failed, but this public reproduction confirms the note.
